steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: Recruit, appoint or assign the core multidisciplinary team from September through November 2026. Mobilise sufficient engineering, integration and quality capacity to protect the King’s Edge roadmap while building the September 2027 Hub release, and confirm how service design, user research and business analysis will be provided alongside the funded core team.

outputs.title: Core team appointments
outputs.summary: Recruit or assign the agreed engineering, integration, quality, product and experience design, and agile delivery capacity.

outputs.title: Experience-discovery capacity
outputs.summary: Confirm named service-design, user-research and business-analysis capacity for first-year Hub discovery and testing alongside product delivery.

outputs.title: Leadership and decision rights
outputs.summary: Confirm who leads the team, how product and technical decisions are made and how capacity conflicts are escalated.

outputs.title: Protected delivery lanes
outputs.summary: Establish explicit capacity protection for the King’s Edge roadmap and the horizontal Hub release within one shared team and pipeline.

outputs.title: Product-owner interfaces
outputs.summary: Define how the team works with the 4.1.2 Hub product and platform owner and the 4.1.4 King’s Edge product owner.

outputs.title: Initial pipeline and capacity plan
outputs.summary: Create one prioritised view of demand, available capacity, sequencing and constraints across Edge delivery, Hub aggregation and discovery.

existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with King’s Edge sponsorship
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide product leadership, institutional prioritisation and resolution of competing demand across 4.1.2 and 4.1.4.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The team may receive conflicting demand or lack authority to protect agreed delivery commitments.

existingCapacity.role: Service design, user research and business analysis
existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with the Student Experience Hub sponsor
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide protected capacity to support priority-integration discovery, student-home prototyping, user research, service blueprinting and cross-service analysis while the core team delivers Edge and the Hub.
existingCapacity.periodNeeded: September 2026 to July 2027, with ongoing involvement thereafter
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The product and experience designer may be spread across interface delivery and institutional discovery, leaving neither sufficiently resourced.

existingCapacity.role: Architecture, data, integration and assurance specialists
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide protected specialist input for identity, source-system integration, data, security, privacy, accessibility, performance and live-service readiness.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The core team may be blocked by specialist queues or reach assurance too late for the September 2027 release.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide named service-management and support counterparts so delivery and live operation are planned together.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The team may deliver capabilities without a credible route into ongoing support.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: Indicative £275,000 in constant 2026 prices for November 2026 to June 2027.
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Three engineering FTE, including at least one strong full-stack or integration focus and hands-on technical leadership, one product and experience designer, 0.5 FTE quality engineering and test automation, and one agile delivery manager. This brings forward the additional integration and quality capacity previously assumed only from Year 2. Service-design, user-research and business-analysis capacity remains additional and must be assigned or costed separately rather than absorbed into the core team.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: A four-person pod would create an avoidable trade-off between the protected King’s Edge roadmap and the September 2027 Hub release, with insufficient resilience for concurrent integration, quality and hardening work.

enablingConditions.condition: Approve the 5.5 FTE first-year team shape and recruitment route in time for recruitment to begin in September 2026.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with King’s Edge sponsorship
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The team will enter the first-year build without enough engineering and quality capacity for the committed scope.

enablingConditions.condition: Assign named specialist contributors with protected availability and clear decision rights.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The core team may be blocked by competing specialist queues.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm protected first-year service-design, user-research and business-analysis capacity before prototypes and alpha testing intensify, using existing or seconded capacity where credible and costing any unresolved gap separately.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with the Student Experience Hub sponsor and Finance
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The Hub may be built as a technical aggregation without sufficient evidence about student use and service design.

enablingConditions.condition: Operate one coordinated product pipeline across 4.1.2, 4.1.3 and 4.1.4, but make the protected capacity for the agreed Edge roadmap and September Hub release visible and subject to explicit trade-off decisions.
enablingConditions.owner: King’s Edge Portfolio Board and Digital and IT
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: One stream may silently consume the capacity required by the other.

steps.title: Establish the product operating model and delivery practices
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish one product operating model with transparent intake, prioritisation and explicit capacity allocation across the protected King’s Edge and Hub delivery lanes, alongside discovery, user research, service design, prototyping, engineering, quality, assurance and release practices.

outputs.title: Demand intake and prioritisation
outputs.summary: Create one transparent route for new demand, triage, sequencing and capacity decisions.

outputs.title: Capacity allocation and trade-off rules
outputs.summary: Make protected commitments visible and require explicit decisions when new demand would displace Edge or the September Hub release.

outputs.title: Discovery and problem definition
outputs.summary: Establish proportionate methods for understanding needs, outcomes, constraints and evidence before committing to solutions.

outputs.title: Continuous user research and co-design
outputs.summary: Build diverse student and staff involvement into discovery, design, testing and evaluation.

outputs.title: Engineering and quality practices
outputs.summary: Agree code review, automated and manual testing, integration quality, technical documentation and maintainability expectations.

outputs.title: Embedded assurance workflow
outputs.summary: Define how the team collaborates with architecture, data, security, privacy, accessibility and service management throughout delivery.

outputs.title: Release and hardening disciplines
outputs.summary: Establish definitions of ready and done, beta exit criteria, scope-freeze rules and the end-of-July feature-complete gate for the first Hub release.

steps.title: Prove concurrent delivery through King’s Edge and the first Hub release
steps.summary: From January to October 2027, prove that one multidisciplinary capability can deliver the protected King’s Edge roadmap and the horizontal Student Experience Hub in parallel. Use repeated discovery, build, integration, quality, assurance, beta, hardening and live-release cycles to refine team roles, capacity allocation and specialist handoffs.

outputs.title: Protected concurrent delivery
outputs.summary: Demonstrate that the team can progress the agreed King’s Edge roadmap and the common Hub release without one silently displacing the other.

outputs.title: Repeated Edge delivery cycles
outputs.summary: Move replatforming and richer Edge capabilities predictably through build, test and controlled use.

outputs.title: Working Hub integration cycles
outputs.summary: Move timetable, KEATS and Ask King’s from integration discovery through prototype, alpha, beta and production readiness.

outputs.title: Continuous student and service involvement
outputs.summary: Show that users and operational owners influence decisions throughout discovery and delivery.

outputs.title: Quality and assurance integrated into delivery
outputs.summary: Use quality engineering, test automation and specialist assurance throughout rather than adding them only after feature build.

outputs.title: September 2027 launch readiness
outputs.summary: Support scope freeze, stress testing, operational rehearsal and production launch of the shared student front door.

outputs.title: Practice and role improvements
outputs.summary: Use delivery evidence to improve the operating model, team shape, workflow and specialist interfaces.

newInvestment.item: Year 2 peak digital product development team
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Continues the 5.5 FTE peak team established in Year 1 through launch, live-service stabilisation, ongoing King’s Edge development and the first deeper Hub roadmap. The profile should be reset against evidence before commitment, particularly the balance between engineering, integration, quality and live-service work.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Capacity may fall away at the point the Hub enters production and the team must support live service alongside the continuing product roadmap.

enablingConditions.condition: Reset the Year 2 staffing profile against the confirmed product pipeline, launch obligations and evidence from the first delivery cycles rather than assuming the role mix remains static.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT product capability leadership with King’s Edge Portfolio Board
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The team shape may not match the confirmed balance of product delivery, integration and live-service work.

steps.title: Make product operations and live-service collaboration routine
steps.summary: From November 2027 to February 2028, make the team’s operating practices routine across the live Student Experience Hub and King’s Edge product domain, balancing roadmap delivery, incidents, maintenance, quality, discovery and continuous improvement.

outputs.title: Routine pipeline and capacity cadence
outputs.summary: Maintain a transparent backlog and regular prioritisation and capacity decisions across product demands.

outputs.title: Predictable discovery and release rhythm
outputs.summary: Establish a repeatable cadence that balances discovery, delivery, quality, release and evaluation.

outputs.title: Live-service feedback loop
outputs.summary: Connect incidents, support evidence, maintenance and service performance directly into product prioritisation.

outputs.title: Ownership and handover model
outputs.summary: Clarify when the team retains responsibility, collaborates with service owners or transfers an enduring capability.

outputs.title: Product evidence and benefits review
outputs.summary: Use product analytics, research and operational evidence to assess value and decide what happens next.

steps.title: Scale the team and its practices across the wider app roadmap
steps.summary: From March to October 2028, apply the established operating model across a growing portfolio of student journeys. Increase throughput and support concurrent work while preserving continuous user involvement, disciplined prioritisation, quality, embedded assurance, learning and sustainable ownership.

outputs.title: Concurrent product delivery
outputs.summary: Support several product demands without fragmenting prioritisation, practices or accountability.

outputs.title: Consistent quality and assurance
outputs.summary: Apply common product, research, design, engineering, quality and assurance expectations across the roadmap.

outputs.title: Professional capability development
outputs.summary: Strengthen role development, mentoring, communities of practice and access to specialist leadership.

outputs.title: Balanced delivery and live-service capacity
outputs.summary: Plan explicitly for new development, maintenance, support, technical improvement and research.

outputs.title: Evidence-led team design
outputs.summary: Refine roles and capacity using throughput, quality, service and demand evidence rather than assumption.

newInvestment.item: Year 3 peak digital product development team
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before the 2028/29 staffing plan is fixed
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Continues the peak team through the final intensive year of wider-app delivery, concurrent live-service work and transition into an enduring capability.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Capacity may taper before the team has supported the principal wider-app transition and embedded sustainable practices.

enablingConditions.condition: Reset the final mobilisation-year staffing profile against the confirmed roadmap, concurrent product demand and live-service responsibilities.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT product capability leadership
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The team profile may not match the work required to deliver and operate the wider app.

steps.title: Embed an enduring institutional product-development capability
steps.summary: From November 2028 to June 2029, establish the multidisciplinary team, its recurrent staffing, professional leadership, governance, product practices and interfaces with product owners and specialist Digital and IT services as an enduring institutional capability.

outputs.title: Recurrent team and funding model
outputs.summary: Confirm the sustainable core staffing and funding route beyond mobilisation.

outputs.title: Enduring governance and decision rights
outputs.summary: Confirm authority over the pipeline, capacity, methods and escalation routes.

outputs.title: Professional leadership and career routes
outputs.summary: Embed role development, professional standards, mentoring and progression for the multidisciplinary team.

outputs.title: Stable specialist and service interfaces
outputs.summary: Confirm how the team works with architecture, data, integration, assurance, service management and product owners.

outputs.title: Continuous-improvement operating model
outputs.summary: Maintain regular discovery, delivery, evaluation and practice improvement after mobilisation ends.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: Indicative £263,000 annual recurrent cost in constant 2026 prices.
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before recurrent budgets and organisational structures are fixed for 2029/30
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Recurrent Digital and IT baseline, TBC
newInvestment.rationale: Retains two full-stack engineers, approximately 0.75 FTE product and experience design and approximately 0.75 FTE agile delivery and product operations.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The institution will lose the multidisciplinary development capability created through mobilisation.

enablingConditions.condition: Approve the 3.5 FTE recurrent team model before the final mobilisation year ends.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with institutional investment governance
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The team may reach the end of mobilisation without a funded route into business as usual.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm enduring product-capability leadership, prioritisation governance and the relationship to the Hub product and platform ownership under 4.1.2.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with the accountable Student Experience Hub sponsor
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before transition to business as usual
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The permanent team may lack clear authority over its pipeline, practices and capacity.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm professional-development and specialist-practice support for the recurrent team.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before transition to business as usual
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The capability may persist as staffing capacity without the professional depth needed to remain effective.
